key_insight: A clustering-based wrapper feature selection method, CSFS, matches sequential feature selection performance while cutting computation for renewable energy prediction.
engineering_relevance: This work helps engineers build faster, more reliable wind and solar forecasting pipelines by automatically selecting the most useful inputs from large sensor and weather datasets.
method: Cluster variables before selection to reduce redundancy.
Apply sequential wrapper selection within clusters using the prediction model.
Compare against SFS, filter methods, and Random Forest feature importance.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated CSFS on wind turbine power curve modeling and photovoltaic power prediction, finding performance comparable to SFS with an average 21% reduction in computational cost.
watch_item: CSFS is still a wrapper method, so its effectiveness depends on the predictive model, the chosen clustering setup, and the representativeness of the training data.
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
